claims.text: International benchmark Brent crude oil fell more than eight per cent to US$88.36 per barrel on July 27 as the United States and Iran paused military strikes.
The United States and Iran resumed hostilities earlier in July after Iranian forces attacked commercial ships passing through Omani waters in the Strait of Hormuz.
The share price of Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT rose 500 per cent on its Shanghai debut after raising US$9.8 billion in its initial public offering.
US President Donald Trump stated that US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth 'has done a great job' amid questions regarding military advice on Iran.
US advisors informed Donald Trump that Iran was actively preparing to attack the United States if Washington did not strike pre-emptively.
US President Donald Trump claimed Iran requested a meeting directly and through surrogates after facing military strikes.
US President Donald Trump stated aboard Air Force One that 'there are very friendly negotiations going on' regarding the conflict with Iran.
Tehran denied engaging in any direct negotiations with the United States regarding the conflict.
The United States and Israel launched joint military strikes against Iran on February 28, 2026.
In June 2026, Iran and the United States signed a memorandum of understanding to halt military operations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Mediators led by Qatar and Pakistan are working to facilitate communications between Washington and Tehran.
Iran-backed armed groups launched drone attacks against targets in Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Iraq following the US-Iran strike pause.
US Central Command redirected 17 commercial vessels, disabled two, and boarded two in the Strait of Hormuz to enforce a naval blockade.
US President Donald Trump warned in an interview with Axios that the US would resume 'very strong military action' against Iran if diplomacy fails.
Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for targeting Saudi petroleum infrastructure, including the East-West Pipeline.
French President Emmanuel Macron described current wildfires as 'completely unprecedented' and the country's 'toughest since World War Two'.
Wildfires have forced the evacuation of 220,000 people in France and more than 100,000 people in Spain.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu reported that 116,085 hectares have burned and 162 arrests related to fire starts have occurred since July 6.
Cestas Mayor Jerome Steffe reported 17,000 residents were evacuated overnight as a wildfire burned 42,000 hectares and destroyed 240 houses in his region.
A wildfire in Ávila, west of Madrid, burned 50,000 hectares, making it the largest recorded wildfire in Spain's history.
Spain's government reported that 172,000 hectares of forested land have burned this year, six times the area burned in 2025.
More than 400 people were evacuated by sea from Italy's Gargano peninsula as a wildfire encroached on beaches in Puglia.
The National Firefighters Federation of France reported that a massive wildfire in southwest France generated a pyrocumulonimbus fire cloud, a phenomenon never previously observed in France.
Bridget Phillipson was appointed Labour party chair, replacing Anna Turley following a UK cabinet reshuffle.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Portsmouth, becoming Burnham's first international guest since taking office.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the UK will share the intellectual property for its 'Stone Cloak' electronic warfare system with Ukraine.
The UK's Stone Cloak electronic warfare jammers are tablet-sized devices designed to prevent drones from being detected.
The United Kingdom has committed £25 billion in funding for Ukraine's military effort since Russia's full-scale invasion four years ago.
Former UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced £255 million in fresh funding for Ukraine during his final visit to Kyiv.
Ed Miliband serves as Foreign Secretary in UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah commended the CRPF on Raising Day for eliminating Left-wing extremism within a March 31, 2026 deadline.
The Central Reserve Police Force launched an inquiry into whether the use of pump-action pellet guns by the Rapid Action Force during July 20 student protests was authorized.
Nearly 47 Rapid Action Force personnel were injured, including six with head injuries and four with fractures, during student protests outside Parliament.
Student activist Aishe Ghosh filed a petition in the Delhi High Court seeking to declare mass facial recognition surveillance of protesters unconstitutional.
Indian Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following student-led demonstrations over national exam paper leaks.
The Rajya Sabha was adjourned for a sixth consecutive day after opposition members demanded Home Minister Amit Shah apologize for police action against protesting students.
Delhi Police alleged that 2,873 individuals present at Jantar Mantar protests had criminal antecedents, identifying 989 using a Facial Recognition System.
The Cockroach Janta Party demanded the withdrawal of all criminal cases filed against demonstrators as part of a negotiated settlement with the Indian government.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called Iranian retaliation threats 'unjustified and groundless', labeling Tehran an accomplice to Russian aggression.
Security Service of Ukraine drones struck an oil platform, a Russian missile boat, and sanctioned cargo vessels in the northern Caspian Sea.
India's Ministry of External Affairs summoned Ukrainian Ambassador Oleksandr Polishchuk to express serious concern over attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea.
Four Indian seafarers were killed and one was critically injured on July 19 during an attack on a cargo vessel departing Odesa port.
Indian Chief Officer Sagar Gupta was killed when the Marshall Islands-flagged MV Omorfi was hit by drones in Russian waters on July 18.
Five Indian seafarers have been killed in the Russia-Ukraine war, with two remaining missing following a July 25 attack on the MV AGN Ragnar.
India summoned Russia's Chargé d'Affaires Vladimir Ladanov following the death of four Indian sailors on the MV Golden Leo on July 19.
India's Ministry of External Affairs issued a formal advisory urging Indian citizens to assess security risks before accepting maritime work in the Black Sea.
